goal: Stack the three coloured cubes into a tower in the bottom-to-top colour order given by the instruction, then return the robot arm(s) to the start pose.
instruction_templates: stack the blocks from bottom to top in the order of {color[block_0]}, {color[block_1]}, and {color[block_2]}, then reset the robot arm.
success: is_stacked with in_order=True, label_list=[block_0, block_1, block_2], xy_threshold=0.0175 m, no z_threshold: block_0 is the bottom, block_1 in the middle, block_2 on top. For each adjacent pair (lower, upper): horizontal (XY) distance between the two object ROOT positions <= 0.0175 m AND (upper root z - lower root z) >= 0.005 m (no upper limit on the z gap).

all_robot_back_to_origin: every target arm's end-effector pose is within 0.15 m per axis (|dx|,|dy|,|dz| each <= 0.15 m) and within 20 degrees (quaternion angular distance) of its start-of-episode pose (the arms must be returned to roughly their starting pose).
evaluation: Success conditions form ONE stage: after every action (once all simulation sub-steps of that action are done) the reward manager evaluates all conditions; the episode succeeds as soon as ALL hold simultaneously at the same moment (reward 1 -> episode ends with success). Conditions are not latched or ordered. Otherwise the episode ends as a failure after step_lim=400 actions (the check made after the last action still counts). No early-fail rule exists apart from the environment being flagged invalid (e.g. a required label missing / physics broken).
objects: block_0, block_1, block_2: three cubes (category 'cube', model indices drawn without replacement from {1 blue, 2 green, 3 red, 7 yellow, 8 orange, 9 cyan}, so three DIFFERENT colours), 3 total, random positions on the table in x in [-0.43, 0.43], y in [-0.25, 0.0] (Table-relative), random yaw within +-45 degrees; a prohibited area rectangle [0.1,-0.23,-0.1,-0.17] is excluded from placement
needs_memory_or_language: Language: the instruction names the colour of the bottom, middle and top block (e.g. 'blue, green, and red'). The solver must identify which cube is which colour (via vision/colour) and map them to block_0 (bottom), block_1 (middle), block_2 (top). Which colour is block_0/1/2 is randomised per episode; the instruction text is generated from the actual cube model indices.
end_requirements: All target (controlled) arms must be back near their start pose when success is evaluated (it is one of the success conditions, see success list): every target arm's end-effector position within 0.15 m on EACH of x, y, z (per-axis, not Euclidean) and orientation within 20 degrees of its pose at the start of the episode (pose recorded right after the robot is set to its initial state). Gripper opening is NOT checked by the success test.
notes: The order matters: with in_order=True the list order is the stacking order, so a correct tower in a different colour order fails (z gap sign checked: upper must be >= 0.005 m above lower). No gripper-open requirement in success (only in the process score). XY tolerance 0.0175 m is on root-to-root distance, i.e. cubes must be quite well centred. A get_score() process score exists (20 for block_0/block_1 stacked within z gap <=0.04 m + gripper open (threshold 0.92 normalised) + block_0 not lifted more than 0.01 m from initial z; 100 for the full tower with gripper open) but does not determine success. Success is evaluated on object root poses/points, not on gripper contact. Object geometry sizes/asset dimensions are not in the source and cannot be determined statically. Instruction template is an f-string: each {color[...]} is replaced by the colour of that block's model index (1 blue, 2 green, 3 red, 7 yellow, 8 orange, 9 cyan).
